title: A Asset for the Contact
premise: August Okonkwo, a veteran interpreter for a collapsing peace delegation, discovers the safe house sheltering his defector contact has been listed online with interior photos — meaning someone inside sold them out. Ordered to extract the defector, Ilya Verhoeven, before the listing's broker collects, August realizes Ilya may be deliberate bait to draw out the mole within their own delegation. As August navigates betrayal by his mentor, a buyer's fixer who offers him a new identity at a terrible price, and the truth that his own twenty years of service were collateral inherited from a father's debt, he must choose between delivering Ilya to save himself or burning every rule he's ever obeyed. In the end, August fakes Ilya's death, hands the delegation the mole, and walks away with nothing but a name that finally belongs to him.
about_author: W. M. Marchetti is a former NGO field translator who spent a decade in contested border regions before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose job is to speak for others and never be heard themselves.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: August, mid-translation at a deadlocked peace summit, idly browses property sites and finds the safe house — his safe house — photographed room by room, Ilya's coat on the hook. POV: August. Beat: cold dread masquerading as professional calm; the moment the story's floor gives way.

chapters.title: Protocol of Silence
chapters.summary: August reports the breach through channels and is told, gently and firmly, to forget it. His mentor, Deputy Director Sable, reassigns him to Ilya's extraction anyway — a favor that smells like a trap. POV: August. Beat: the loneliness of being managed rather than heard.

chapters.title: Ilya, Waiting
chapters.summary: Inside the safe house, Ilya Verhoeven has packed one bag and memorized the listing's photos, knowing exactly which camera angles betrayed him. He tells August the sale isn't a leak — it's an invitation. POV: Ilya. Beat: wary mutual sizing-up; two men fluent in distrust.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: August's first posting, his father's unexplained debts, the mentorship under Sable that saved him and owned him. POV: August. Beat: elegiac; the reader learns August's survival has always been rented, never owned.

chapters.title: The Broker's Card
chapters.summary: The realtor who listed the house turns out to be Vess, a fixer for an unnamed buyer, who approaches August openly: deliver Ilya, and receive a clean identity, money, erasure. POV: August. Beat: temptation rendered as courtesy; the offer is almost kind.

chapters.title: Route Planning
chapters.summary: August and Ilya plan extraction through the old delegation corridors, but every route August knows is one Sable taught him. Ilya quietly notes this aloud. POV: Ilya. Beat: creeping paranoia; trust built and immediately taxed.

chapters.title: The Delegation Eats Itself
chapters.summary: The peace summit collapses publicly; a leaked memo accuses the delegation of harboring assets it never declared. August realizes Ilya's defection was never secret — it was leverage someone planned to spend. POV: August. Beat: institutional betrayal; the rules rewrite themselves mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Sable's Debt
chapters.summary: August confronts Sable, who admits the safe house was exposed to force the extraction — and reveals the debt that binds August is his father's, inherited, twenty years of service as interest. POV: Sable. Beat: devastating clarity; August learns he was always the asset.

chapters.title: Night Market
chapters.summary: A tense interlude: August and Ilya move through a border city's night market to buy false papers from an old contact who once loved August's father. POV: August. Beat: fragile warmth and grief; the past surfaces in a stranger's kindness.

chapters.title: The Contact's Ledger
chapters.summary: The papers-forger shows August his father's old ledger: names, payments, and Sable's signature from before August was born. The inheritance theme crystallizes — August was collateral before he was a man. POV: August. Beat: rage and vertigo; identity as inherited debt.

chapters.title: Vess Again
chapters.summary: Vess corners August with a deadline and a detail only the buyer could know: the exact wording of August's childhood nightmares. The buyer has been reading him his whole life. POV: August. Beat: intimate horror; the enemy knows him better than his allies.

chapters.title: Ilya's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilya admits he may be bait and doesn't know for whom — his defection was brokered by someone he never met, and his value may be as a lure for August himself. POV: Ilya. Beat: mutual honesty at last; two assets comparing chains.

chapters.title: The Safe House Burns
chapters.summary: The safe house is torched the night before extraction; August and Ilya escape through the listing's own photographed escape route — the one detail the photos revealed and the buyers dismissed. POV: Ilya. Beat: adrenaline and grim irony; the surveillance becomes salvation.

chapters.title: Hunted by the Handbook
chapters.summary: Pursuers use August's own training manuals to predict his movements; he must improvise against himself, breaking every rule he ever taught. POV: August. Beat: the self as antagonist; liberation through incompetence.

chapters.title: Sable's Choice
chapters.summary: Sable intercepts them, gun drawn, and offers August one last chance to deliver Ilya and inherit his father's position — clean, powerful, permanent. August sees his entire future in the offer and refuses. POV: August. Beat: the thesis moment; identity over inheritance.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Table
chapters.summary: August walks, alone, into the buyer's meeting — a face from the delegation's founding generation, the man who wrote the rules his father died under. POV: August. Beat: quiet dread; the architecture of the whole conspiracy revealed in one room.

chapters.title: A Death, Manufactured
chapters.summary: August proposes a trade: a body, a fire, a confirmed kill — Ilya dead on paper, the buyer's prize delivered, the mole in the delegation exposed as the buyer's own man. POV: August. Beat: the interpreter finally authors the text instead of translating it.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: The staged death goes wrong; Vess, ordered to clean up loose ends, turns instead on the buyer, and Sable takes a fatal bullet shielding August — the mentor's last, unpayable debt repaid. POV: Ilya. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, and the collapse of every inherited obligation.

chapters.title: What the Mole Signed
chapters.summary: August hands the delegation the buyer's ledger — including his father's page and his own — detonating the scandal that ends the delegation and frees every name in it. POV: August. Beat: scorched-earth justice; inheritance converted to evidence.

chapters.title: Ilya, Departing
chapters.summary: Officially dead, Ilya boards a freighter under a name August forged for him — the first document August ever authored for someone's freedom rather than someone's use. POV: Ilya. Beat: bittersweet parting; two men who taught each other to want.

chapters.title: The Name on the Door
chapters.summary: August declines reassignment, resigns, and for the first time registers a name, an address, a life that no one else drafted. The property site still lists safe houses; he closes the tab. POV: August. Beat: quiet, hard-won ownership of self.

chapters.title: Interpreter, Former
chapters.summary: Months later, August translates freelance — wedding vows, asylum interviews, nothing classified — and receives a postcard from Ilya: a photo of a house, no listing, no price. POV: August. Beat: resolution; the price of survival paid in full, and worth it.
